name: Masauyra Curry
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a pan and lightly fry the masauyra balls until golden brown; set aside.
2. In the same pan, sauté chopped onions until translucent.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
4. Stir in tomatoes and powdered spices (turmeric, chili, cumin, coriander) with a splash of water, cooking until the oil separates.
5. Add the fried masauyra balls and enough water to create a gravy consistency.
6. Cover and simmer until the lentil balls are soft yet hold their shape.
7. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice.
description: Masauyra is a traditional Sikkimese staple made from fermented and sun-dried lentil balls. It is a vital protein source in the mountain diet, known for its distinct umami flavor and chewy texture, commonly prepared during the winter months when fresh produce is scarce.
